entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Arvind Kumar,Sharda Vishwakarma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The instant anticipatory bail application has been moved by the applicant for enlarging him on bail in Case Crime No.543 of 2024, under Sections 420, 406, 504 & 506 I.P.C., Police Station Naini,
District Prayagraj.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Applicant challenged the FIR by filing Criminal Misc.Writ Petition No.17110 of 2024 (Chandra Sen Singh @ Chandra Sen Vishwakarma) and the Division Bench of this Court has passed the following orders on 23.09.2024:-
Chandrasen Vishwakarma vs State Of U.P. on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165262171/

sentences.text: 1 "1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned AGA for the State.

2. Although, the prayer made in this writ petition is to quash the First Information Report dated 30.08.2024, giving rise to Case Crime No.0543 of 2024, under Sections 406, 420, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station - Naini, District Prayagraj, but at the time when the matter is taken up learned counsel for the petitioners confines his relief to grant of protection under section 35 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

3. We have perused the the First Information Report, which prima facie discloses commissioning of cognizable offence and, therefore, the prayer made to quash F.I.R.
otherwise cannot be entertained in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of State of Telangana Vs. Habib Abdullah Jellani, (2017) 2 SCC 779 and Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra and Others, (2021) SCC Online SC 315.
4. We are of the view that no interference is warranted.
5.

sentences.text: However, considering the fact that all offences, mentioned in the present case, are punishable with a term up to 7 years, therefore, authorities are directed to ensure the procedure of arrest as per the guidelines of Supreme Court enshrined in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273 as well as the directions issued in judgment and order dated 28.01.2021 of this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.17732 of 2020.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
6. The writ petition, accordingly, is disposed of."
4.

Since the Division Bench of this Court had directed the authorities to ensure the procedure of arrest as per the guidelines of Supreme Court enshrined in the case of Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014)8 SCC 273 but the Investigating Officer by telephonic call unnecessarily summoned the applicant and threat to implicate the applicant on another case.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014)8 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA further submitted that the Division Bench of this Court had passed orders in pursuance of guidelines of Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar (Supra).
Till today no charge-sheet has been submitted.
Submission of the applicant is false and not supported by any evidence.
Applicant would have to appear before the Investigating Officer if he summoned for the purposes of investigation.
5. The relief as sought by the applicant through this application is refused.
6. Considered the argument of both the parties.

The instant anticipatory bail application is disposed of with the direction that the Investigating Officer in pursuance of Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar,
shall record statement after giving notice under section 41A Cr.P.C. & 35 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 and shall proceed with the case in accordance with law.
Order Date :- 12.3.2025 SKD
